subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs default to delete-after-run cleanup, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` remain invalid and be rejected?
rationale: Both directions are represented by open PRs, and the choice changes cron lifecycle semantics, upgrade behavior, and user-visible session retention.

options.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Revise this PR or a replacement so new and existing omitted isolated recurring jobs clean up safely, with load or doctor migration proof.

options.title: Reject recurring delete-after-run
options.body: Pause or close this PR and pursue the one-shot-only validation direction after its caller and upgrade gaps are fixed.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Land only the new-job default and explicitly accept that existing omitted jobs require operator action or separate migration.

recommendation.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Revise this PR or a replacement so new and existing omitted isolated recurring jobs clean up safely, with load or doctor migration proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the adjacent cleanup implementation that defines the runtime behavior once `deleteAfterRun` is true.
